questions.questionText: Your company needs to migrate 500 TB of archival data from an on-premises data center to Google Cloud Storage. The data center has a very slow internet connection, and calculating the transfer time over the network results in an estimate of over a year. Which data transfer solution should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Transfer Appliance is a high-capacity hardware device that you rack in your data center, fill with data, and physically ship to Google. It is the standard solution for migrating massive amounts of data when network bandwidth is too low or latency is too high for online transfers.

why other options are wrong.Storage Transfer Service: Storage Transfer Service performs online transfers over the network. It would be bottlenecked by the slow internet connection.
why other options are wrong.gsutil command-line tool: The gsutil CLI tool transfers data over the network and would take over a year on a slow connection.
why other options are wrong.Dedicated Interconnect: While Dedicated Interconnect provides high bandwidth, provisioning a physical dedicated fiber connection just for a one-time archival migration is overly expensive and complex compared to a Transfer Appliance.

questions.questionText: You are hosting thousands of static images in a Cloud Storage bucket located in the US. Users in Asia are experiencing high latency when loading these images. What is the easiest way to configure the system to reduce image load latency for global users?
options: Enable Cloud CDN on an External Application Load Balancer in front of the bucket.
Change the bucket location to a Multi-region bucket.
Migrate the images to a Cloud SQL database.
Configure Turbo Replication on the Cloud Storage bucket.
correctAnswers: Enable Cloud CDN on an External Application Load Balancer in front of the bucket.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud CDN caches static content at Google's global edge locations (points of presence) physically close to users. By placing an External Application Load Balancer in front of your bucket and enabling Cloud CDN, users in Asia will download images from an edge cache in Asia, drastically reducing latency.

why other options are wrong.Change the bucket location to a Multi-re: A multi-region bucket in the US still serves data from the US, which does not solve the latency problem for users in Asia.
why other options are wrong.Migrate the images to a Cloud SQL databa: Relational databases are not designed to serve static image files efficiently and would increase latency and costs.
why other options are wrong.Configure Turbo Replication on the Cloud: Turbo Replication ensures dual-region buckets replicate data within 15 minutes for disaster recovery; it does not cache data globally for end-user latency.

questions.questionText: You are configuring a Compute Engine instance that will run a data processing job requiring the absolute lowest possible storage latency and highest IOPS. The data is temporary and does not need to be saved after the VM restarts. Which storage option should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Local SSDs are physically attached to the server hosting the virtual machine instance. Because they bypass the network, they provide the lowest latency and highest Input/Output Operations Per Second (IOPS) available, making them perfect for ephemeral scratch space.

why other options are wrong.Extreme Persistent Disk: Extreme PD provides very high IOPS, but it is still a network-attached persistent disk, so it has higher latency than a physically attached Local SSD.
why other options are wrong.Standard Persistent Disk: Standard PDs use traditional HDD storage over the network, resulting in high latency and low IOPS.
why other options are wrong.Filestore: Filestore is a managed NFS file server accessed over the network, which introduces network latency.

questions.questionText: Your company mandates a daily, automated data transfer from a specific Amazon S3 bucket into Google Cloud Storage for disaster recovery purposes. Which Google Cloud service is designed to handle this securely and automatically without custom coding?

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service allows you to configure scheduled, automated, and secure online transfers of objects from Amazon S3, Azure Storage, or on-premises file systems directly into Google Cloud Storage.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service automates moving data into BigQuery for analytics, not moving objects into Cloud Storage.
why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: This is an offline hardware device used for massive one-time migrations, not for daily automated syncing.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: While Dataflow could theoretically be coded to do this, it requires writing custom Apache Beam code, whereas Storage Transfer Service is a fully managed, code-free configuration.

questions.questionText: To provide the lowest possible network latency for global users transferring data to your cloud applications, which Network Service Tier should you configure for your external IP addresses?

explanation.general explanation: The Premium Network Tier routes traffic over Google's highly reliable, low-latency global fiber network. User traffic enters Google's network at an edge point of presence (PoP) closest to the user, ensuring the lowest latency for data transfer.

why other options are wrong.Standard Tier: Standard Tier routes traffic over the public internet, only entering Google's network at a PoP close to the region where your application is hosted, resulting in higher latency.
why other options are wrong.Enterprise Tier: There is no Enterprise Tier in Google Cloud networking.
why other options are wrong.Global Tier: There is no Global Tier; the tiers are named Premium and Standard.

questions.questionText: Your monolithic application reads data from a Cloud SQL for MySQL database. The database is suffering from high latency because thousands of users are running the exact same 'view catalog' read queries simultaneously. Which two configurations can you implement to reduce this read latency? (Select two)
options: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica.
Implement Memorystore for Redis as a caching layer.
Change the database storage type to Standard HDD.
Configure a Cloud SQL High Availability (HA) standby instance.
correctAnswers: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica.
Implement Memorystore for Redis as a caching layer.

explanation.general explanation: To reduce latency caused by heavy read traffic, you can offload those reads. A Cloud SQL Read Replica allows you to distribute read queries across multiple instances. Implementing an in-memory cache like Memorystore for Redis allows the application to serve frequent read queries in sub-milliseconds without hitting the database at all.

why other options are wrong.Change the database storage type to Stan: HDDs are significantly slower than SSDs and would increase database latency.
why other options are wrong.Configure a Cloud SQL High Availability: An HA standby instance is used strictly for failover during an outage. It cannot be actively queried to offload read traffic.

questions.questionText: You configured a Dual-region Cloud Storage bucket to protect critical data. The business requires a strict Recovery Point Objective (RPO) guarantee that all new data transfers will be replicated to the secondary region within 15 minutes. Which feature must you enable?

explanation.general explanation: Turbo Replication is a feature for dual-region Cloud Storage buckets that guarantees 100% of newly written objects are asynchronously replicated to the secondary region within 15 minutes, ensuring a strict, financially backed RPO.

why other options are wrong.Object Versioning: Object Versioning protects against accidental deletion or modification by keeping old versions; it does not speed up cross-region replication.
why other options are wrong.Storage Transfer Service: STS is for batch transferring data between buckets or clouds, not real-time synchronous/asynchronous replication for a single dual-region bucket.
why other options are wrong.Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS): CORS is an HTTP security protocol for web browsers accessing resources across different domains.

questions.questionText: You are using the Google Cloud CLI (`gcloud storage` or `gsutil`) to transfer hundreds of extremely large video files from your local workstation to Cloud Storage over a high-bandwidth connection. What is the easiest way to configure the CLI tool to maximize transfer speed and utilize all available bandwidth?
options: Zip all the files into a single archive before uploading.
Change the storage class of the destination bucket to Nearline.
Use a VPN tunnel instead of the public internet.

explanation.general explanation: Parallel composite uploads split large files into smaller chunks, upload them in parallel, and then compose them back together in Cloud Storage. This heavily saturates available network bandwidth and drastically reduces transfer times for large files.

why other options are wrong.Zip all the files into a single archive: Zipping them makes one massive file, which without parallel uploads would transfer linearly and slower.
why other options are wrong.Change the storage class of the destinat: The storage class has no impact on the network ingestion speed or data transfer rate.
why other options are wrong.Use a VPN tunnel instead of the public i: A VPN adds encryption overhead and can actually reduce maximum throughput due to gateway bandwidth limits.

questions.questionText: Your Compute Engine virtual machines in `us-central1` frequently read and process raw data files. To minimize latency during this data transfer process, what location type should you configure for the Cloud Storage bucket holding the raw data?
options: A Multi-region bucket in the US.
A Dual-region bucket in us-east1 and us-west1.

explanation.general explanation: To achieve the lowest possible latency and the highest throughput, compute resources (like VMs) and storage resources (like Cloud Storage buckets) should be co-located in the exact same region. A Regional bucket in `us-central1` provides the best performance for VMs in `us-central1`.

Data in a multi-region bucket is dispersed. Fetching it may involve cross-region network hops, which adds slight latency compared to a strictly local regional bucket.
why other options are wrong.A Dual-region bucket in us-east1 and us-: Neither of these regions matches the compute region, introducing cross-region latency.
This would introduce massive transatlantic network latency.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud services or tools are optimized specifically for transferring large volumes of data into Cloud Storage over an active online network connection? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service is a managed service for online batch transfers. The `gcloud storage` or `gsutil` CLI tools are heavily optimized for fast, multi-threaded online data transfers from local machines or VMs to Cloud Storage.

why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: Transfer Appliance is an offline hardware device, not an online network transfer tool.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service moves data into BigQuery, not into Cloud Storage.

questions.questionText: An enterprise wants to transfer massive amounts of data from their on-premises SAN to Google Cloud Storage. They have a strict requirement that the data transfer must bypass the public internet entirely to ensure minimum latency and maximum security. Which connectivity option must be configured?

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct, physical fiber connection between your on-premises network and Google's network. It bypasses the public internet completely, offering the highest bandwidth and lowest latency for data transfer.

why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: Cloud VPN securely encrypts traffic, but it routes that traffic over the public internet.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering: VPC Peering connects two Google Cloud VPC networks internally; it does not connect on-premises data centers.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows internal cloud VMs to reach the public internet; it is not a private hybrid cloud connection.

questions.questionText: You are building an Internet of Things (IoT) application that ingests millions of small data events per second. The data storage system must process these writes with consistent sub-millisecond latency. Which storage system should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Bigtable is Google Cloud's NoSQL wide-column database. It is heavily optimized for extremely high throughput and consistent sub-millisecond latency for massive read/write workloads, making it the standard choice for IoT and time-series data ingestion.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a relational database and cannot scale to millions of writes per second with sub-millisecond latency.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage is an object store. While it handles high throughput, it does not provide sub-millisecond latency for millions of tiny discrete database writes.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner offers strong global consistency, but its standard write latency is in the single-digit milliseconds, not sub-millisecond, and it is overly complex for simple IoT time-series ingestion compared to Bigtable.

questions.questionText: Your application relies on rapid, repetitive lookups of player session states. To achieve the absolute lowest latency for data retrieval, which in-memory data store service should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Memorystore for Redis is a fully managed in-memory data store service. Because data is stored entirely in RAM, it provides sub-millisecond data access, making it the fastest option for caching session states and reducing read latency.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner reads from persistent disk storage, which has higher latency than in-memory RAM.
why other options are wrong.Firestore: Firestore is a NoSQL document database reading from persistent storage, not an in-memory cache.
why other options are wrong.Local SSD: Local SSD is physical block storage. While very fast, reading from disk still incurs higher latency than reading directly from RAM via Memorystore.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud connectivity solutions provide a dedicated, private network connection from an on-premises data center to Google Cloud, ensuring low-latency data transfers that bypass the public internet? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect and Partner Interconnect both provide direct, private, physical connections to Google Cloud. These connections do not traverse the public internet, ensuring consistent, low-latency, high-bandwidth data transfers.

why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: Cloud VPN secures traffic but routes it over the unpredictable public internet.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows internal instances to access the internet; it does not connect on-premises data centers.

questions.questionText: Two separate departments in your company have their own Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks. They need to transfer large datasets between their respective Compute Engine VMs. What is the most secure configuration to achieve the lowest possible latency for this data transfer?
options: Configure VPC Network Peering between the two VPCs.
Set up a Cloud VPN tunnel over the public internet between the two VPCs.
Assign public IP addresses to all VMs and communicate externally.
Use Cloud NAT to route traffic from one VPC to the other.
correctAnswers: Configure VPC Network Peering between the two VPCs.

explanation.general explanation: VPC Network Peering connects two VPCs natively within Google Cloud's internal infrastructure. Traffic routes using private internal IP addresses, bypassing the internet entirely, which provides the highest bandwidth and lowest latency for data transfers between VPCs.

why other options are wrong.Set up a Cloud VPN tunnel over the publi: VPN adds encryption overhead and internet routing, increasing latency.
why other options are wrong.Assign public IP addresses to all VMs an: This exposes VMs to the internet, degrades security, and incurs external egress data transfer charges.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud NAT to route traffic from one: Cloud NAT is for outbound internet access, not for peering internal private networks.

questions.questionText: Your marketing team wants to automatically transfer daily campaign performance data from third-party SaaS applications (like Salesforce and Google Ads) directly into BigQuery for reporting. Which configuration avoids manual scripting?
options: Configure the BigQuery Data Transfer Service.
Set up a Storage Transfer Service job.
Write a Cloud Function to pull the API hourly.
correctAnswers: Configure the BigQuery Data Transfer Service.

explanation.general explanation: The BigQuery Data Transfer Service automates data movement into BigQuery on a scheduled basis. It natively supports pulling data from Google SaaS applications (like Google Ads) and external SaaS applications (like Salesforce) without writing custom code.

Storage Transfer Service moves files into Cloud Storage, not structured data from SaaS APIs into BigQuery.
This is an offline hardware device, unsuitable for daily, automated API data transfers.
why other options are wrong.Write a Cloud Function to pull the API h: While possible, this requires manual coding and maintenance, which the prompt specifically seeks to avoid.

questions.questionText: When planning your cloud budget for data storage and network architectures, you need to account for data transfer costs. In Google Cloud, transferring data INTO a Cloud Storage bucket is generally free. What is the technical term for the data transfer traffic that incurs network charges when users download data from Google Cloud?

explanation.general explanation: Network 'Egress' refers to data traffic leaving the Google Cloud network (e.g., a user downloading a file to their local computer). While ingress (data entering GCP) is typically free, egress traffic is billed based on volume and destination.

why other options are wrong.Ingress: Ingress is data entering the cloud, which is generally free.
why other options are wrong.Throughput: Throughput is the rate of data transfer (speed), not the billing classification for outbound data.
why other options are wrong.Latency: Latency is the delay in network communication, not a term for data transfer volume.

questions.questionText: You are designing a globally distributed web application. The application requires a relational database that can provide strongly consistent reads with low latency for users located in different continents. Which database service is explicitly designed for this global, low-latency architecture?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner is a fully managed, globally distributed relational database. It is designed to automatically replicate data across multiple regions, providing strong global consistency and low-latency access for users regardless of their geographic location.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a regional relational database. It does not provide global, active-active multi-region read/write capabilities out-of-the-box.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Bigtable: Cloud Bigtable is a NoSQL database, not a relational database.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore: Memorystore is a regional in-memory cache, not a globally distributed relational database.

questions.questionText: Your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters require a shared file system. To ensure fast data transfer and low latency file access across hundreds of Pods simultaneously, which storage service should you mount?

explanation.general explanation: Filestore provides fully managed, high-performance Network File System (NFS) storage. It is designed specifically for low-latency file operations and can be mounted simultaneously by multiple GKE Pods.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage using HTTP API: Cloud Storage is an object store accessed via HTTP, which has significantly higher latency for standard file system operations than NFS.
why other options are wrong.Local SSD: Local SSDs cannot be shared across multiple nodes in a GKE cluster.
why other options are wrong.Zonal Persistent Disk: A standard Persistent Disk in ReadWriteOnce mode can only be mounted by a single node at a time.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud databases natively support active multi-region configurations, automatically replicating data globally to ensure low-latency reads for distributed users? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner (relational) and Firestore (NoSQL document) are both globally distributed databases. They natively support multi-region configurations to replicate data across continents, minimizing read latency for global audiences.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a regional database service. Setting up cross-region replicas is manual and not natively active-active.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore for Redis: Memorystore provides zonal and regional high availability, but does not natively provide automatic global multi-region replication.

questions.questionText: A virtual machine hosted on Compute Engine is running a database that requires high IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second). The disk is currently a Standard Persistent Disk (pd-standard). What is the easiest way to significantly reduce disk latency and increase data transfer throughput to the disk?
options: Upgrade the disk type to an SSD Persistent Disk (pd-ssd) or Extreme Persistent Disk.
Format the disk with a different file system.
Move the VM to a different zone.
correctAnswers: Upgrade the disk type to an SSD Persistent Disk (pd-ssd) or Extreme Persistent Disk.

explanation.general explanation: Standard Persistent Disks use traditional spinning hard drives (HDDs), which have high latency. Upgrading the disk to an SSD Persistent Disk (pd-ssd) or an Extreme Persistent Disk provides solid-state storage, dramatically reducing latency and increasing IOPS/throughput.

why other options are wrong.Format the disk with a different file sy: File systems do not overcome the physical hardware latency of underlying HDDs.
Moving to another zone does not change the performance characteristics of a standard HDD.
Cloud Storage is an object store accessed over HTTP, which has much higher latency than block storage.

questions.questionText: You want to enable Cloud CDN to cache media files stored in a Cloud Storage bucket, ensuring low latency for public users. To configure Cloud CDN, what networking component MUST you place in front of the Cloud Storage bucket?
options: An Internal Passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: Cloud CDN works by attaching to a backend. To serve content from a Cloud Storage bucket via Cloud CDN, you must configure the bucket as a backend for an External Application Load Balancer (HTTP/S).

why other options are wrong.A Cloud Router: Cloud Router is for BGP dynamic routing over VPN/Interconnect, not for web traffic caching.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud NAT Gateway: Cloud NAT allows internal VMs to access the internet; it does not serve cached content to external users.
why other options are wrong.An Internal Passthrough Network Load Bal: Internal load balancers are not exposed to the public internet and do not support Cloud CDN.

questions.questionText: You are designing a data pipeline that uses Compute Engine VMs to transfer massive amounts of data. In Google Cloud Compute Engine, what hardware configuration strictly dictates the maximum network egress bandwidth (data transfer speed) limit of a virtual machine instance?
options: The number of vCPUs assigned to the VM.
The amount of RAM assigned to the VM.
The size of the boot disk.
The Google Cloud region the VM is deployed in.
correctAnswers: The number of vCPUs assigned to the VM.

explanation.general explanation: In Compute Engine, maximum network egress bandwidth scales linearly with the number of vCPUs. To achieve higher data transfer speeds out of a VM, you must provision a machine type with more vCPUs.

RAM dictates memory capacity, not network throughput limits.
Disk size dictates disk IOPS and throughput, not network bandwidth limits.
why other options are wrong.The Google Cloud region the VM is deploy: Network limits are tied to machine architecture (vCPUs), not the geographic deployment region.

questions.questionText: You need to migrate 10 TB of log files from an on-premises Hadoop cluster directly into Google Cloud Storage over your existing high-speed VPN connection. Which managed service should you configure to securely transfer this data?

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service allows you to configure agents on your on-premises servers to securely transfer unstructured data (like log files from a Hadoop cluster) over the network (via VPN or Interconnect) directly into Cloud Storage.

why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: Transfer Appliance is a physical device used for offline transfers when network bandwidth is too slow, which contradicts the 'high-speed VPN' prompt.
why other options are wrong.Database Migration Service: DMS is for structured relational databases, not flat log files.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: Dataflow is for processing data, not primarily for basic file migration. While it could be forced to do this, STS is the correct managed tool.

questions.questionText: Which two configurations heavily influence the network latency and data transfer speed when downloading a file from a Google Cloud Storage bucket to a user's local computer? (Select two)
options: The geographic location of the bucket relative to the user.
The Network Service Tier (Premium vs. Standard) configured for the application.
The Storage Class (Standard vs. Archive) of the bucket.
Whether Object Versioning is enabled on the bucket.
correctAnswers: The geographic location of the bucket relative to the user.
The Network Service Tier (Premium vs. Standard) configured for the application.

explanation.general explanation: Network latency is fundamentally bound by physics (distance); thus, the geographic location of the bucket relative to the user is the primary factor. Secondly, the Network Service Tier determines whether the data travels over Google's fast private backbone (Premium) or the slower public internet (Standard).

why other options are wrong.The Storage Class (Standard vs. Archive): In Google Cloud Storage, all storage classes (including Archive) have the same sub-second time-to-first-byte latency.
why other options are wrong.Whether Object Versioning is enabled on: Object versioning keeps historical copies of files; it does not affect the speed of the network transfer.

questions.questionText: Google Cloud's global network uses an advanced TCP congestion control algorithm by default to maximize data transfer bandwidth and minimize latency across the internet. What is the name of this algorithm?
options: TCP BBR (Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time)
correctAnswers: TCP BBR (Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time)

explanation.general explanation: TCP BBR (Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time) is a congestion control algorithm developed by Google. It significantly improves network throughput and reduces latency for data transfer on Google Cloud's network compared to traditional algorithms like CUBIC or Reno.

why other options are wrong.TCP CUBIC: This is a standard default for many Linux distributions but is not the optimized proprietary algorithm developed and highlighted by Google for GCP.
why other options are wrong.TCP Reno: This is a very old legacy TCP congestion algorithm.
why other options are wrong.TCP Tahoe: This is another legacy TCP congestion algorithm.

questions.questionText: You have a local directory of log files on your on-premises server that updates continuously. You want to execute a CLI command that only transfers the new or changed files into a Cloud Storage bucket, avoiding the latency of re-uploading the entire directory. Which command should you use?

explanation.general explanation: The `rsync` command within the Google Cloud CLI (`gcloud storage rsync` or `gsutil rsync`) compares the source and destination directories. It only transfers data that is new or has changed, saving significant bandwidth and transfer time.

why other options are wrong.`gcloud compute scp`: This command copies files to a Compute Engine VM via SSH, not to a Cloud Storage bucket.
why other options are wrong.`gsutil cp -R`: The copy (`cp`) command with the recursive flag will blindly copy the entire directory again, wasting bandwidth and time.
why other options are wrong.`gcloud storage cat`: The `cat` command outputs the contents of a file to the terminal; it does not synchronize directories.

questions.questionText: You need to configure disaster recovery for your application. You want to replicate a 10 TB Cloud Storage bucket from the `us-central1` region to a completely separate bucket in the `europe-west1` region securely and efficiently. Which configuration is the easiest way to manage this data transfer?
options: Configure a Storage Transfer Service job between the two buckets.
Write a Cloud Function to copy files triggered by Object Finalize events.
Download the data to a local VM and upload it to the new bucket.
correctAnswers: Configure a Storage Transfer Service job between the two buckets.

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service is not just for external data; it is also the managed, optimal tool for transferring data between two different Cloud Storage buckets within Google Cloud, handling retries, scaling, and synchronization automatically.

why other options are wrong.Write a Cloud Function to copy files tri: While possible for new files, it requires custom coding and does not handle the existing 10 TB of data easily.
why other options are wrong.Download the data to a local VM and uplo: This introduces a massive bottleneck (the VM's network adapter) and unnecessary egress/ingress latency.
DMS is for relational databases, not Cloud Storage buckets.

questions.questionText: Your application ingests a continuous stream of financial transactions. Instead of landing the data in storage and processing it in batches (which introduces latency), you want to process and transform the data in real-time as it transfers through the system. Which service should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Dataflow is Google Cloud's fully managed service for stream and batch data processing. By processing data in real-time streams (in-flight) rather than waiting for batch uploads, you drastically reduce the latency between data ingestion and actionable insights.

why other options are wrong.Storage Transfer Service: STS simply moves files from A to B; it does not process or transform data streams.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage Autoclass: Autoclass manages storage billing tiers based on access frequency, unrelated to stream data processing.
why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: This is a physical offline hardware device, the exact opposite of real-time stream processing.

questions.questionText: Users in London are querying a Cloud SQL database physically located in `us-central1`. They are complaining of high network latency during data retrieval. You cannot move the primary database out of the US. What is the standard architectural configuration to reduce read latency for these users?
options: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica in the `europe-west2` (London) region.
Enable Cloud CDN in front of the Cloud SQL database.
Change the database storage disk to Extreme Persistent Disk.
Configure the Cloud SQL instance to use a Multi-region Cloud Storage bucket.
correctAnswers: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica in the `europe-west2` (London) region.

explanation.general explanation: Creating a cross-region Read Replica in London allows the database to asynchronously replicate data closer to the users. When European users perform read queries, they hit the local replica, completely eliminating the transatlantic network latency.

why other options are wrong.Enable Cloud CDN in front of the Cloud S: Cloud CDN caches HTTP/S web traffic, not direct TCP relational database connections.
why other options are wrong.Change the database storage disk to Extr: A faster disk speeds up local query execution, but does not solve the physics of transatlantic network latency.
why other options are wrong.Configure the Cloud SQL instance to use: Cloud SQL manages its own block storage; it does not use Cloud Storage buckets for its primary operational data.
